description: PCI DSS 4.0 compliance overlay — cardholder-data tokenization via Stripe, PAN redaction middleware, secure-delete helpers, CHD-scoped audit logs. Composes onto ecommerce-headless / api-service.

buildHints.whenToUse: Adding PCI DSS 4.0 primitives (CHD tokenization, PAN redaction) to a commerce backend. Reduces SAQ scope when paired with Stripe Checkout.
firstSteps: Use Stripe Checkout or Stripe Elements — CHD never touches your servers. This pack's tokenize.ts wraps Stripe's createPaymentMethod.
Wire `redactPan()` from `src/pan-redact.ts` onto every log + error tracer. One raw PAN in Sentry = SAQ failure.
Audit log scope: only CHD-access events go to the PCI audit store; general app audit stays in its own store.
Never store full PAN, CVV, or PIN. If you need to reference a card, store the Stripe payment_method id (`pm_...`) — it's a token, not CHD.
gotchas: CVV must NEVER be stored post-authorization — PCI DSS 3.2.1 prohibits it. Even in encrypted form.
PAN in URL query strings is a violation — always POST.
Test card numbers in fixtures (e.g. 4242...) still count as CHD in the scope assessment. Quarantine test data.
Stripe's restricted key patterns: use a restricted key scoped to PaymentIntents only for server-side code; never ship the full secret key.
DO NOT log request/response bodies on payment endpoints without redaction — the log sink often ingests them unfiltered.

placeholders.description: PAN-redaction regex. Extend for BINs your processor uses outside the standard Luhn range.
